item.content:encoded:
Chief Justice Sir Gibbs Salika has challenged the people and leadership of West Sepik to maintain their exemplary record of law and order if they hope to secure a permanent resident judge in Vanimo.

Speaking at the official inauguration of the Supreme Court's first-ever sitting in the province, Sir Gibbs responded directly to a request from the provincial governor for a residential judge. While indicating he would consider posting a judge to Vanimo, the Chief Justice stressed that judicial presence should not replace local responsibility.

"Yes, we do cater for judges and magistrates to be based in provinces," Sir Gibbs said. "But it is also our duty to ensure that West Sepik Province maintains law and order to a level where we do not need police officers, correctional officers, and lawyers to be based here."

The historic sitting marks the first time in 50 years of Independence that Supreme Court cases will be heard on home soil in West Sepik.

Sir Gibbs was accompanied to Vanimo by Justice Minister and Attorney-General Pila Niningi, alongside seven judges of the National and Supreme Courts, to witness the occasion.

Sir Gibbs revealed that West Sepik accounts for only 15 of the nearly 1,200 active cases before the Supreme Court, commending the province’s reputation as one of the nation's most peaceful,

Justice Colin Makail reinforced the statistics, praising the local population for setting a high standard for the rest of Papua New Guinea.

"As of July 24, 2026, the Supreme Court has 1,196 cases, comprising 500 criminal and 648 civil," Justice Makail revealed. "Out of this, West Sepik has only 15 cases, all of which are criminal, with zero civil cases registered."

Justice Makail urged the people of West Sepik to maintain their law-abiding reputation as the highest court in the land begins its work in the province.

item.title: New ICT minister Robert Naguri takes office with focus on employee welfare
item.description: Newly appointed Minister for Information and Communications Technology [ICT] and Member for Bogia, Robert Naguri, has assured staff across the sector that employee welfare will be his top priority. Speaking at the official handover ceremony on Monday at the National Broadcasting Corporation [NBC] headquarters, Minister Naguri emphasized that employee well-being directly impacts performance.
item.content:encoded:
Newly appointed Minister for Information and Communications Technology [ICT] and Member for Bogia, Robert Naguri, has assured staff across the sector that employee welfare will be his top priority.

Speaking at the official handover ceremony on Monday at the National Broadcasting Corporation [NBC] headquarters, Minister Naguri emphasized that employee well-being directly impacts performance.

The ICT ministry oversees three key entities in the Department of Information and Communications Technology [DICT], the National Information and Communications Technology Authority [NICTA], and the NBC.

“Your welfare is very important to me. When you are happy and enjoying your job, you will give the nation 100 percent,” Naguri said.

He acknowledged outgoing Minister and Member for South Bougainville, Timothy Masiu, thanking him for his service and committing to build on the groundwork already laid.

Masiu served as ICT minister since 2019, leading key reforms and developments in the sector from broadcasting space to vital legal framework and pivotal infrastructure changes.

“The outgoing minister has done a lot over the past six years. I cannot achieve everything he has achieved in just eight months, but the foundation is already there, and I will continue where my brother left off,” The new minister said.

Naguri said he will meet with agency heads to delegate key responsibilities effectively to meet the expectations set by the Prime Minister.

The new minister also extended his gratitude to the Regional Member for Bougainville, Peter Tsiamalili Jr., for his leadership and support over the past 12 months as acting ICT minister.

Naguri urged staff across all three institutions to foster mutual respect, open communication, and teamwork to drive the department forward.

Outgoing Minister Timothy Masiu expressed full confidence in the new minister, calling on all department heads and staff to extend their total support to minister Naguri.

item.title: Unitech says no new campus breach after weekend scare
item.description: The Papua New Guinea University of Technology says there was no new security breach during a weekend incident that caused fear among students. The university said campus security received a report at about 10.27pm on Saturday from the University Adventist Residential College [UARC] about possible criminal activity near the campus.
item.content:encoded:
The Papua New Guinea University of Technology says there was no new security breach during a weekend incident that caused fear among students.

The university said campus security received a report at about 10.27pm on Saturday from the University Adventist Residential College [UARC] about possible criminal activity near the campus.

Security officers were sent to UARC and the Catholic Residential College. While responding, they saw a commotion outside the university boundary in a nearby community.

The university said there was no attempt to enter the campus, breach the perimeter fence or damage university property.

The incident came a week after an alleged break-in at the UARC girls' dormitory and left many students, especially female students, frightened.

Some male students moved towards the female residential areas to offer support. The university said this, along with uncertainty about what was happening, added to the confusion on campus.

Vice-Chancellor Professor Ora Renagi said the university had held its second security meeting in a week to respond to students' concerns.

"The management made it very important to ensure that we restore security and provide a secure study and living environment," he said.

Professor Renagi said the university was working closely with police, government and other partners to improve security.

He said every report from students was taken seriously. Security officers searched the residential colleges and surrounding areas to make sure there were no unauthorised people inside the dormitories.

The university said it had already increased security around student residences, stepped up overnight patrols, strengthened perimeter monitoring and improved coordination with the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary.

Deputy Prime Minister and Lae MP John Rosso said more security measures would be introduced.

"Your safety is paramount and we'll do everything possible," he said.

Police are continuing to investigate the alleged break-in at the UARC girls' dormitory on 18 July.

One suspect has surrendered to Lae's Criminal Investigation Division, while police continue to search for the remaining alleged offenders.

The university says it will continue working with police to keep students and staff safe.

item.title: Supreme Court officially opens circuit in Vanimo after nearly 50 years
item.description: In a landmark moment for West Sepik, the Supreme Court of Papua New Guinea officially opened its circuit sittings in Vanimo on Monday, marking the first time in nearly 50 years that the country's highest court has sat in the province. item.content:encoded:
In a landmark moment for West Sepik, the Supreme Court of Papua New Guinea officially opened its circuit sittings in Vanimo on Monday, marking the first time in nearly 50 years that the country's highest court has sat in the province.

The official opening was led by Chief Justice Sir Gibbs Salika, accompanied by seven judges of the National and Supreme Courts in Justice Collin Makail, Justice Kenneth Frank, Justice Thomas Anis, Justice Vergil Narokobi, Justice Paul Tusais, Justice Rebecca Christensen, and Justice Jeffrey Mesa. They were joined by Chief Magistrate Mark Pupaka and resident magistrates.

The historic ceremony was attended by Minister for Justice and Attorney-General Pila Niningi, West Sepik Governor Tony Wouwou, Minister for Tourism, Arts and Culture and Vanimo-Green River MP Belden Namah, and Aitape-Lumi MP Anderson Mise, along with provincial leaders and members of the legal fraternity.

In welcoming the judicial delegation, Namah described the occasion as a significant achievement for the people of West Sepik after decades without Supreme Court sittings in the province.

"For many of our people, travelling from Vanimo to Port Moresby to access Supreme Court services is costly and difficult. Bringing the Supreme Court to Vanimo makes justice more accessible and affordable for our people," he said.

In his keynote address, Chief Justice Salika said West Sepik is widely regarded as one of Papua New Guinea's more peaceful provinces. He said while resident judges are often assigned to areas experiencing high crime rates, West Sepik has maintained a relatively peaceful environment and does not face overwhelming levels of criminal activity.

Justice Makail reflected on the history of the judiciary in Sandaun, revealing that the National Court first sat in Vanimo on 1 October 1975, only weeks after PNG gained Independence. Court records show that the inaugural National Court sitting was held at the site where the Indonesian Consulate now stands.

The commencement of regular Supreme Court circuit sittings in Vanimo represents a major step towards decentralising judicial services, improving access to justice, reducing travel costs, and strengthening the rule of law for the people of the border province.

item.title: Poverty driving crime rise: Supt
item.description: Population growth and widespread economic hardship are the primary drivers behind the recent surge in criminal activities in Morobe’s capital, police say. Lae Metropolitan Superintendent Chris Kunyanban said police investigations revealed a concerning shift in local crime trends, where offenders are moving away from stealing cash and high-value items, targeting basic survival necessities like food
item.content:encoded:
Population growth and widespread economic hardship are the primary drivers behind the recent surge in criminal activities in Morobe’s capital, police say.

Lae Metropolitan Superintendent Chris Kunyanban said police investigations revealed a concerning shift in local crime trends, where offenders are moving away from stealing cash and high-value items, targeting basic survival necessities like food and clothing instead.

Met Supt Kunyanban said the trend directly reflects the level of poverty and hardship currently affecting urban families.

He said recent criminal activities have increasingly involved teenagers, young children, and women.

Following instances of public retaliation, Kunyanban issued a warning to residents against taking the law into their own hands when apprehending suspects.

"We have laws that can protect you, therefore, please do not take the law into your own hands," he said.

He warned criminals that the public is now hyper-aware of their activities and urged them to refrain from lawlessness.

The police boss said Lae residents are growing weary of ongoing opportunistic crime and are beginning to take community ownership to minimize and eradicate mischief in their suburbs.

Kunyanban called on local communities to work directly with the police force, suggesting the establishment of neighborhood watch programs. He also urged state institutions and commercial properties to install functional closed-circuit television [CCTV] systems to boost security monitoring.

Meanwhile, police investigations are underway into the recent breaking and entering incidents at two higher education institutions in PNG University of Technology [Unitech] and the National Polytechnic Institute of Papua New Guinea.

item.title: Rosso leads Unitech security response
item.description: Deputy Prime Minister and Lae MP John Rosso has stepped in to strengthen security at the Papua New Guinea University of Technology after an alleged armed break-in at the University Adventist Residential College [UARC] girls’ dormitory. Mr Rosso says protecting students and staff is the priority. He has announced more police patrols, security upgrades and a review of weak areas around the campus.
item.content:encoded:
Deputy Prime Minister and Lae MP John Rosso has stepped in to strengthen security at the Papua New Guinea University of Technology after an alleged armed break-in at the University Adventist Residential College [UARC] girls’ dormitory.

Mr Rosso says protecting students and staff is the priority. He has announced more police patrols, security upgrades and a review of weak areas around the campus.

He visited the university with Lae Metropolitan Commander Chief Superintendent Chris Kunyanban, Superintendent Operations James Luan and Lae Chamber of Commerce and Industry chairman John Bryn.

The team met with the PNGUoT Council, senior management, police and security officers before inspecting the affected girls’ dormitory and parts of the campus fence.

Mr Rosso said students must feel safe while studying at the university.

“We have got to make certain that the students who come here are sitting in a safe, secure environment. And not only the students, also the faculty members who reside here.”

He said police would increase their presence on campus and support the university security team.

The measures include retraining security officers, improving lighting, installing CCTV cameras and strengthening patrols around areas considered vulnerable.

A police vehicle will also be stationed near the girls’ dormitory during overnight hours.

“The police will take them back and retrain them, and see if we can assist with arming them, so that they can provide an armed response with regular members of the police force.”

Mr Rosso also warned criminal groups, including those known as OBT, saying authorities would not ignore the threat they pose to communities.

“They are now preying on the vulnerable... we cannot just turn a blind eye. We have to address this seriously.”

He said his response was also based on his experience in policing and security.

Mr Rosso said PNGUoT covers more than 50 hectares, making security difficult, but urgent action was needed.

“The immediate thing now to do is to safeguard our female students and try to safeguard all the rest of the university faculty.”

The university says it will continue working with police, government and other partners to improve security and provide a safe place for students and staff.

item.title: Crusade inspires hundreds in Wewak

item.content:encoded:
More than 700 Christians from Wewak Urban and surrounding sub-districts gathered at the AOG Full Gospel Town Church in Wewak, East Sepik Province, for the Indoor Mega Crusade with renowned USA Evangelist Randy Jach from 25–27 July 2026.

Held under the theme “Equipping the Harvesters” from Matthew 9:37–38, the three-day crusade encouraged believers to strengthen their relationship with God and be ready to serve in His harvest.

Evangelist Jach shared that he traveled for five days from the United States to Papua New Guinea to preach the Gospel. In his final message, he encouraged Christians to practise five key disciplines: fast one day each week, pray one hour daily, read and study the Bible for 10 minutes every day, faithfully give one-tenth [tithe], and faithfully give offerings.

He said these five principles have guided his life and ministry, opening doors for him to preach in 131 countries over the past two years. Wewak was his first stop in Papua New Guinea before traveling to Port Moresby to continue his preaching.

Evangelist Jach thanked Senior Pastor Ivan Lesly for finding him online and inviting him to minister in Wewak. He reminded the congregation not only to hear God’s Word but to put it into action.

Speaking on behalf of the church board, church elder Freddy Benguma thanked Evangelist Jach for accepting God’s call to travel to Wewak. The church board and leaders also presented him with gifts in appreciation of his ministry.

The AOG Full Gospel Town Church in Wewak holds a special place in the history of the AOG movement, as it is where the first AOG missionaries arrived before spreading the Gospel to other districts in East Sepik Province.

item.title: NIPS ends boat mishap recovery
item.description: A 48-hour extended recovery operation by the New Ireland disaster office will conclude today, though local communities are on alert for any further sightings. The New Ireland Provincial Government on Sunday handed over six more bodies in Kavieng, bringing the total number of repatriated victims to 13, while 14 others remain missing at sea.
item.content:encoded:
A 48-hour extended recovery operation by the New Ireland disaster office will conclude today, though local communities are on alert for any further sightings.

The New Ireland Provincial Government on Sunday handed over six more bodies in Kavieng, bringing the total number of repatriated victims to 13, while 14 others remain missing at sea.

During the official handover ceremony, New Ireland Governor Byron Chan, accompanied by Provincial Administrator Richard Andia and New Ireland Provincial Disaster Coordinator, Terence Tasia, formally handed over the bodies to East New Britain Governor Michael Marum.

Governor Chan conveyed his deepest condolences on behalf of the people of New Ireland and said the province stands with East New Britain during this difficult time. He also assured the province of New Ireland's support and said it is ready to help whenever disaster strikes.

To support relief and custom protocols, the New Ireland Provincial Executive Council presented East New Britain with K70,000 in financial assistance alongside traditional shell money [mis], delivered by chief executive officer of Economic Sector Edward Lasisi.

Accepting the assistance, Governor Marum thanked the people and volunteers of New Ireland for handling the deceased with immense dignity, respect and care.

Marum presented K10,000 directly to the local search and rescue volunteers, promising a formal thank you ceremony once all recovery efforts and formal proceedings conclude.

The tragic boat accident happened on Saturday, July 18, in East New Britain waters, where 27 lives were claimed.

According to New Ireland Provincial Disaster Coordinator, Terence Tasia, the first five bodies were recovered in the Tigak group of islands on Wednesday, July 22. Four more were found in the same area on Thursday, and a teenager's body was recovered on Salapiu Island on Friday, July 25. Three female bodies were among those recovered off Djaul Island.

item.title: East Sepik cocoa farmers receive organic fertilizers to boost production
item.description: Cocoa farmers across East Sepik Province are taking another step towards increasing cocoa production following the rollout of an organic fertilizer distribution program supported by the East Sepik Governor's Office and the Cocoa Board of Papua New Guinea.

item.title: Queen of Paradise Orchestra students embark on international music journey
item.description: Two pioneering students from the Queen of Paradise Orchestra in Vanimo are set to begin an exciting new chapter in their musical journey after being accepted to study classical music in the Philippines.
